title: Traffic-aware probe tuning and token-bandwidth SLO for private VPC workers
creator: Avery Chen
description: Goal: introduce a traffic-aware health probe and SLO definition that measures token-bandwidth capacity per private VPC worker (edge and dedicated-snowballs), ties probe thresholds to latency SLO budgets, and provides Terraform modules + rollout hooks to safely enable this across customer VPCs. Motivation: current saturation sensors focus on absolute CPU/GPU utilization and token throughput windows; they do not account for request size distribution (tokens per request) or per-worker egress limits, which leads to noisy shedding during mixed workloads and unsafe upgrade rollouts. Deliverables: 1) PromQL/Flux probe definitions for 'token_bandwidth_consumption' normalized by worker_shape and seq_len_percentiles; 2) a new Terraform module (redwood_vpc_probe_token_bandwidth) that exposes configurable percentiles, alert windows, and automatic remediation policies; 3) console dashboard panels and automated canary gating rules (canary pass/fail threshold) for upgrades; 4) a migration plan and rollout playbook for enabling probes without customer-visible throttling.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Avery Chen: RFC posted. Basic approach: compute token_bandwidth = tokens_emitted / active_seconds, normalize by worker GPU_type and qps, use 95th percentile over 5m as probe. Proposed thresholds derived from historical traces in /dashboards/vpc-token-bandwidth. Asking infra for sample traces and limits per instance type.

2026-03-11 - Diego Ramirez: Spiked PromQL query against staging metrics: sum(rate(tokens_emitted[1m])) by (worker) / max(1, avg_over_time(active_sec[5m])) gives useful signal but noisy on bursty traffic. Proposal: incorporate request-size buckets and apply EWMA smoothing (alpha=0.3). Will add synthetic low-QPS probe to validate smoothing.

2026-03-12 - Priya Nair (SRE review): Reviewed probe semantics. Concern: using a per-worker absolute threshold breaks multi-tenant hosts. Recommendation: express thresholds as a fraction of measured capacity per-worker and add cross-worker aggregation to detect hotspots. Added dependency on ENG-27654 to reuse token pressure backoff logic.

2026-03-14 - Diego Ramirez: Prototype Terraform module at github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules/PR-482 merged to branch 'token-bandwidth-probes'. Module exposes inputs: percentile_window, smoothing_alpha, burst_tolerance, remediation_action (log/scale-up/shed). Manual canary run on staging-privy showed stable behavior for chat workloads; observed ~7% reduction in tail-latency during transient traffic spikes when shedding was applied before CPU saturation. Next: write rollout playbook and create console gating for canary rollouts (A/B).
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module published and versioned in infra-modules with docs and examples
PromQL/Alert definitions reviewed and added to vpc-observability repo
Console canary gating shows green for 3 sequential canary runs on staging with mixed request-size workloads
Rollout playbook describing safe enabling, rollback steps, and customer communication completed
implementation_notes: Probe signal: tokens_emitted per second per worker, broken down by request_token_bucket (0-32,33-128,129-512,>512) and normalized to worker_capacity_estimate
Thresholds: dynamic fraction of measured capacity (default 0.82 for P95 window) and separate instantaneous emergency threshold at 0.95
Smoothing: EWMA alpha default 0.3; windowed P95 over 5m for gating decisions
Remediation actions: prefer scale-up for dedicated pools, soft-shed (5-15% traffic) for shared workers, full shed only as last resort
Terraform hooks: pre-upgrade probe-disable flag and post-upgrade probe-validation step to avoid false positives during rolling restarts
